title: Bootstrap Layout
summary: Explains Bootstrap's container / row / col structure, the 12-column sizing classes, the responsive breakpoints and how to combine several breakpoint classes on one element. Three online exercises (appbrewery.github.io/bootstrap-layout) ask the learner to match a demo's behaviour at each breakpoint by adding col classes; the solution is walked through with trial and error.

concepts.heading: Container, row, column
points: Three nested pieces: a div.container as the starting point, a div.row inside it, and one or more column divs inside the row.
A bare class="col" on several children makes Bootstrap share the row width equally: six cols get a sixth each, three get a third each.
The container is responsive: its max width changes with the viewport width (roughly 540px on phones, 720 or 960px on tablets, about 1000px+ on desktops, bigger still on wide screens).

container-{breakpoint} (container-sm, container-md, container-lg, container-xl, container-xxl) is 100% wide below that breakpoint and behaves like a normal container at and above it. Plain container is the same idea as container-sm.
container-fluid is 100% wide at every size, edge to edge. In practice container and container-fluid are the two used most: container for margins at the sides, fluid for edge-to-edge.
All these widths refer to the viewport width only.

concepts.heading: Sized columns (12-column system)
points: Think of each row as 12 equal slots. col-2, col-4, col-6 etc. say how many slots an element occupies, from col-1 to col-12. Bootstrap turns that into a percentage: col-6 is 50%, col-2 is one sixth.
Example: three divs with col-2, col-4, col-6 fill a full row (2 + 4 + 6 = 12) with no custom CSS.
Typical use: a navigation column of 2/12 beside main content of 10/12.
Totals above 12 push the extra column onto the next row. Totals under 12 leave empty space.
Mixing is allowed: two sized columns (col-2, col-4) plus a plain col means the plain col takes whatever remains.

concepts.heading: Breakpoints
points: Predefined widths based on common devices: sm (576px and up), md (768px and up), lg (992px and up), xl (1200px and up), xxl (1400px and up). Below 576px is the extra-small range, which has no infix in class names. Rough device mapping: sm phones, md tablets, lg laptops, xl desktops, xxl very large screens.

Infix classes are min-width based: col-sm-4 applies from the small breakpoint upward. Each class keeps applying at all larger sizes until another class overrides it. Layouts therefore go small first and are tweaked upward.
Below the smallest breakpoint class used, columns default to full width (stacked), as for col.
Using col-sm-4 on three elements means three per row from 576px, and stacked on narrower screens.
Bootstrap's breakpoints reduce the need to write media queries by hand.

One element can carry several breakpoint classes: for example col-lg-4 col-md-8 col-sm-12 gives 4/12 on large screens, 8/12 on medium and full width on small. Narrower screens usually get larger elements for readability.
(Extra) Bootstrap 5 writes this as col-12 col-md-8 col-lg-4; the unprefixed col-12 covers the smallest range, so col-sm-12 is only needed if you want a distinct step at sm.
Layout docs: the Layout section of the Bootstrap docs covers breakpoints, containers, columns and the grid system.

concepts.heading: Solutions to the three online exercises
points: The practice site shows a demo at the top and an editable HTML block below; after editing, press apply changes and resize the window to compare with the demo at each breakpoint.
Exercise 1: 50% on desktop, 100% on mobile. Add col-xl-6 to both divs (6/12 = 50% at 1200px and up). Below that the default is full width, so adding col-sm-12 is optional.

Exercise 2 (columns that change at lg and sm): at lg and above, 6/3/3 gives col-lg-6, col-lg-3, col-lg-3. Between sm and lg, first column full width and the other two half each, so the first column has no sm class and the others get col-sm-6. At the smallest size, each column takes 10 of 12 (found by trying 8, seeing it was too narrow, then 10). So a plain col-10 on each.
Exercise 3 (two columns, five widths): xxl 1 and 11 (col-xxl-1, col-xxl-11); xl 2 and 10; lg 4 and 8; md 6 and 6; below md both full width (an sm class would be redundant).
Each pair of numbers adds up to 12 so both columns stay on one row.
Method: start at the largest breakpoint, estimate proportions by eye (or with a ruler), apply, then step down. Trial and error is fine.
Finding breakpoint widths: in Chrome DevTools toggle the device toolbar, choose Responsive and drag the width bar while watching the pixel number, e.g. a jump at 1200px indicates xl.

task.name: Bootstrap layout practice site (appbrewery.github.io/bootstrap-layout)
task.starting_point: Online page with three exercises, each showing a demo area on top and an editable HTML snippet for your area underneath.
task.goal: Add Bootstrap grid classes so your area reacts to window width exactly like the demo at every breakpoint.
steps: Open the practice site and read the description of exercise 1: 50% width on desktop, 100% on mobile.
Edit the HTML using col-{breakpoint}-{n} classes; press apply changes.
Resize the window and compare with the demo at each breakpoint; use DevTools responsive mode to see the pixel width.
Repeat for exercise 2 (columns that change at lg and sm, and a narrow-screen width) and exercise 3 (two columns, proportions changing at xxl, xl, lg, md).
Check the Layout section of the Bootstrap docs if stuck.
task.expected_result: Your area is indistinguishable from the demo as the window shrinks through each breakpoint.

solution_code.code:
<!-- Ex1 -->  col-xl-6 on both
<!-- Ex2 -->  [col-10 col-lg-6] [col-10 col-sm-6 col-lg-3] [col-10 col-sm-6 col-lg-3]
<!-- Ex3 -->  [col-md-6 col-lg-4 col-xl-2 col-xxl-1] [col-md-6 col-lg-8 col-xl-10 col-xxl-11]

pitfalls: Forgetting that breakpoint classes mean that size and above, not just that size.
Column numbers that do not add to 12 wrapping to a new row unexpectedly.
Missing the row wrapper: cols must sit in a row, which sits in a container.
Giving up on trial and error; matching a target by eye and adjusting is a normal workflow.
(Extra) The exercise solutions above for 2 and 3 are reconstructed from the spoken walkthrough, so verify against the practice site. No reference repo folder exists for this lecture.
